Key observations from the test image:
- Split/dissected soybean stems showing internal tissue
- Bleached white/pale stem appearance
- Large, irregular **black masses** (sclerotia) embedded within the stem tissue
- Dry, dead stem material

This strongly suggests **White Mold** (black sclerotia inside bleached white stems). Let me confirm with reference images.

The Fusarium reference (top-right quadrant) shows a nearly identical visual pattern to the test image — split stems with large black masses. However, comparing against known biology:

- **White Mold** description: "characteristic **black sclerotia** embedded within white mold on stems and **inside stems**; dry dead stems develop a **bleached white appearance**" — this is an exact match
- **Fusarium**: produces reddish-brown vascular discoloration, not large sclerotia
- The large, irregular black bodies in the test image are classic Sclerotinia **sclerotia** inside bleached, hollow stems

The Fusarium reference collage appears to include at least one image showing White Mold symptoms (possibly a dataset overlap), but the diagnostic pathology clearly points to White Mold.

Let me view a few more references to be thorough.
Rhizoctonia and Septoria clearly don't match. I've now viewed 10 reference images. Let me view 2 more to meet the minimum.

Neither matches. I've now viewed 12 reference images.

**Summary of evidence:**

- **Test image**: Split/dissected soybean stems showing bleached white tissue with **large, irregular black masses** (sclerotia) embedded inside
- **White Mold** description: *"characteristic black sclerotia embedded within white mold on stems and inside stems; dry dead stems develop a bleached white appearance"* — **exact match**
- The Fusarium reference collage (top-right) visually resembles the test image, but Fusarium produces vascular discoloration, NOT sclerotia — those images likely show White Mold co-occurrence or mislabeling
- Charcoal Rot has tiny microsclerotia (charcoal dust), not large irregular black bodies
- No other class matches the large black sclerotia + bleached white stem combination
